h1: The 6 Best 5FT Portable Wheelchair Ramps of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 five-foot portable wheelchair ramps scored on stated capacity, rise range, fold size and surface grip for homes and vehicles.
summary: The HYUNAN METHOD is our top 5 ft ramp because it publishes weight, folded size, rise range and an 800 lb capacity. The FACHNUO black all-weather model is the pick for a ramp that lives outdoors. FODINGHILL is the easiest to grab by the center handle, and the VEVOR is the value choice for steps under 10 inches. Whatever you choose, measure the rise first: a 5 ft ramp is only gentle on a 5 inch step.
intro: The most common mistake with a 5 ft ramp is buying it for the length and ignoring the rise. Accessibility guidance works out to about 12 inches of ramp for every inch of height, so a 60 inch ramp is a comfortable climb on a 5 inch step and a hard push on a 15 inch one. Several listings advertise a 5 to 15 inch range, and the top of that range is steep for a manual chair.

We reviewed six folding aluminum ramps from the spec sheets and listing details, scoring each on stated capacity, rise range, folded size, surface grip and how much the listing actually tells you. Two listings do not state a capacity at all, and that gap cost them places. Ramp weight was only published for one model, so we weighted it where we could.

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 5FT Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: The only ramp here that states weight, folded size, rise range and capacity in full.
products.description:
The HYUNAN METHOD opens to 60 x 29 x 2.4 in, folds to 30 x 14.5 x 3.2 in, weighs 26.01 lb and lists an 800 lb capacity. Those figures let you check a trunk, a closet and your own door threshold before ordering.

It beats the FACHNUO black ramp because the carry weight is published, and a ramp you cannot lift is a ramp you stop using. Its 5 to 15 in rise range matches the FACHNUO support-leg model, but the HYUNAN adds the capacity number that model leaves out.

Buy it for a porch step or curb you can measure. The caveat is slope: at 15 in of rise a 60 in span climbs roughly 1 in 4, so keep it to low steps for manual chairs.
cons: Steep at the top of the range
Listing does not describe grip surface
products.idealFor: Caregivers who need a ramp for a measured porch step and want every dimension confirmed in advance.
products.skipIf: Your threshold is 12 to 15 in high and the chair user pushes manually.

products.name: FACHNUO 5FT Black All-Weather Ramp
products.verdict: A stainless center hinge and striped non-slip notches built for ramps that stay outside.
products.description:
This FACHNUO leans on weather-ready details: a stainless steel center hinge, striped non-slip notches across the deck and orange warning signs on the sides. Capacity is listed at up to 800 lb.

The hinge is the reason it outranks the FODINGHILL for outdoor storage, since the hinge is the first part of a folding ramp to corrode or loosen. It sits below the HYUNAN only because the listing leaves out a rise range and carry weight, two numbers you need before you buy.

It suits a ramp left near a back door or garage all year. Confirm the rise with the seller, because this listing does not state one.
products.idealFor: Households keeping the ramp outdoors or in a garage through every season.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed rise range or carry weight before committing.

products.name: FODINGHILL 5FT Folding Aluminum Ramp
products.verdict: Folds in half around a reinforced center handle for easy lifting in and out of a car.
products.description:
The FODINGHILL folds in half, making the package about 50 percent smaller, and carries a reinforced center handle. The title cites 800 lb, and the edges are raised with wrap-around reflective strips.

It ranks third because the handle placement is smarter than the HYUNAN's published dimensions are useful: a centered grip balances the load, which matters for the hip and shoulder of whoever lifts it. It trails the FACHNUO black model on corrosion protection, since no hinge material is described.

Best for caregivers loading a ramp into a trunk daily. The surface is smooth aluminum with a rough coating, so check that coating stays gritty after a season of use.
products.idealFor: Caregivers lifting the ramp into a vehicle every day.
products.skipIf: You want a grooved or notched deck rather than a coated one.

products.name: VEVOR 5FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: A grooved aluminum deck with a sensible 5 to 10 in rise limit at a lower price.
products.description:
The VEVOR fits rises of 5 to 10 in, uses a grooved aluminum deck with a coating, adds raised side baffles with reflective strips, and cites 800 lb in the title.

Its rise ceiling is the honest part. Capping at 10 in keeps the slope near 1 in 6 at worst, gentler than the 15 in ratings on the HYUNAN and FACHNUO support-leg ramp. It drops below FODINGHILL because no fold size or handle detail is given.

Choose it for a porch step or short curb under 10 in. If your threshold is taller, a wider rise range elsewhere in this list serves you better than forcing this one.
cons: Rise range tops out at 10 in
products.idealFor: Low porch steps and curbs under 10 in on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: Your step or van floor is taller than 10 in.

products.name: FACHNUO 5FT Ramp with Support Legs
products.verdict: Support legs under the span and baffles on the sides, but no stated capacity.
products.description:
This FACHNUO opens to 60 x 29 x 2 in, folds to 30 x 14.5 x 6.3 in, and recommends a 5 to 15 in rise. Support legs sit under the span, with baffles and reflective strips along the edges.

The legs are the draw: they take load off the middle of the deck at steeper heights, which the plain folding ramps here cannot do. It lands fifth because the listing never states a capacity, and the 6.3 in folded depth is double the HYUNAN's 3.2 in.

Pick it for taller thresholds near the top of the rise range. Ask the seller for the rated load first, since a ramp without that number is a gamble.
products.idealFor: Taller steps where extra mid-span support is welcome.
products.skipIf: You need a documented weight rating before buying.

products.name: VNN 5FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: Part of a 3 to 8 ft family with a double non-skid deck, but missing key numbers.
products.description:
The VNN is a folding aluminum ramp with a double non-skid surface, and the 5 ft size belongs to a family spanning 3 to 8 ft. Neither the rise range nor the capacity appears in the listing text.

That family is the reason to look: if you later need a longer ramp for a taller step, the same maker offers it. It ranks last because every other ramp here states at least a capacity or a rise range, and this one states neither, so you cannot size it safely from the page.

Buy only after confirming rise and rated load with the seller. For a bare listing this is the least checkable option.
products.idealFor: Buyers who may need a longer ramp from the same line later.
products.skipIf: You need rise and capacity confirmed on the listing page.

methodology.title: Stated load capacity
methodology.description: Ramps with a published rating outrank those without one, since a missing number cannot be verified.

methodology.title: Rise range and slope
methodology.description: We judge whether the stated rise range makes sense for a 60 in span, rewarding listings that keep the slope reasonable.

methodology.title: Portability
methodology.description: Folded size, carry weight and handle design decide how easily one person can move the ramp.

methodology.title: Surface and edge safety
methodology.description: Non-slip texture, raised baffles and reflective strips reduce slips and wheel drift off the sides.

methodology.title: Listing transparency
methodology.description: Every missing spec is a risk for the buyer, so complete listings score higher.

whatMatters.detail: Rise is the vertical height from ground to threshold. A 60 in ramp is gentle at 5 in and steep at 15 in, because the slope doubles and triples. Measure your step with a tape, then compare it to the rise range on the listing, favoring the low end for manual wheelchairs.

Capacity is the total load the ramp should carry, including chair, rider and any gear. A scooter plus rider adds up faster than people expect. Look for a stated figure such as 800 lb, and treat a listing with no number as unrated until the seller confirms it.

The ramp must fit your trunk and be liftable by whoever carries it. Folded dimensions tell you whether it fits behind a seat, and a published weight tells you the real carry burden. Only the HYUNAN lists a weight, so ask for it elsewhere.

Wheels and shoes slip on wet aluminum, so the deck texture matters more outdoors than any other feature. Grooves, striped notches and coated grit each grip differently. Check the description for the pattern, and plan on checking the surface after a season of rain.

Raised baffles keep a wheel from drifting off the side, and reflective strips make the ramp visible at night. Skimping here is a real risk for new chair users. Look for the words baffles or raised edges on the listing, and for reflectors if you use it after dark.

howToChoose.intro: Rise decides everything on a fixed 5 ft ramp, so start with your measured step.

cards.label: Support legs
cards.text: Legs under the span, as on the FACHNUO support-leg model, share load at taller heights but add folded bulk at 6.3 in deep.

cards.label: Plain fold
cards.text: Plain folding decks such as the HYUNAN and FODINGHILL pack slimmer and carry easier, and fit most single steps.

howToChoose.note: Default to a plain fold like the HYUNAN METHOD unless your step sits near the top of the rise range.

howToChoose.intro: Traction differs by deck pattern, and the pattern shows how each ramp handles rain.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Single Porch Step Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A rise range that covers your measured step at its low end, a published capacity and a folded size that fits your storage spot.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The HYUNAN METHOD covers all three, and the VEVOR is the cheaper choice if the step is under 10 in.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The ramp will stay outdoors year round, where the FACHNUO black ramp's stainless hinge and notched deck earn their premium.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need it for a short, occasional step, where the VEVOR or FODINGHILL cover the job at the lower tier.

faq.q: Can a 5 ft ramp handle a 12 inch step?
faq.a: Physically it spans it, but the slope is about 1 in 5, far steeper than the 1 in 12 guideline. The HYUNAN METHOD and FACHNUO support-leg model allow up to 15 in, though a power chair or an assistant is far safer at that grade.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying for length instead of rise. A 5 ft ramp is only gentle on a 5 in step. Measure the threshold first, then pick a model like the VEVOR with a rise limit that fits your height.

faq.q: Is the VEVOR worth it over the HYUNAN METHOD?
faq.a: Only for steps under 10 in. The VEVOR is cheaper and keeps the slope moderate, but it does not publish weight or folded size. The HYUNAN costs a little more and answers every sizing question up front.

faq.q: How do I set one up safely?
faq.a: Place it so the top edge sits flush with the threshold, with no gap, and keep both sides on level ground. Models with baffles, like the FODINGHILL, still need you to keep the wheels centered on the deck.

faq.q: How should I maintain a folding aluminum ramp?
faq.a: Wipe grit from the hinge and rinse the deck after wet weather. The FACHNUO black ramp has a stainless center hinge that resists rust, but any ramp deserves a check of the surface texture each season.

faq.q: Can I use a 5 ft ramp for a scooter into a van?
faq.a: Check the van floor height first, since vehicle thresholds can exceed 15 in. Without a stated capacity, the VNN and FACHNUO support-leg listings need written load ratings before they carry a scooter and rider.

finalTake: The HYUNAN METHOD is the safe default because every number you need to plan a purchase is on the page. The FACHNUO black ramp is the one to buy if it lives outside, and the VEVOR is the sensible low-step budget pick. Avoid any listing that states neither capacity nor rise, and measure your step before you click.
